$note: Nightly batch as a Nebius Serverless Job. The entrypoint is the same jobs/nightly.js the 'Run now' button drives through runProofRun(), so the scheduled and interactive paths cannot drift apart.
name: proofrun-nightly
description: Discover, audit, redesign, verify and draft for a batch of prospects overnight. Writes to file-based memory and generates the Morning Brief. Sends nothing.

container.$image_note: Built from the repository Dockerfile, on mcr.microsoft.com/playwright which already carries Chromium and its system libraries.

resources.$resources_note: No GPU. Inference is served by Token Factory over the API; this container runs Playwright, which is the memory-hungry part. Chromium needs roughly 1GB per context and the batch runs them one at a time.

$timeout_note: A verified run averages 135s in demo mode and 210s against a live site that used all three repair attempts. Four prospects plus the brief fits comfortably; the cap exists so a hung page cannot bill all night.

retry.$retry_note: Deliberately 1. jobs/nightly.js already catches per-prospect failures and continues, so a job-level retry would re-audit prospects that already succeeded and write duplicate drafts.

schedule.$schedule_note: 07:00 Pacific, so the Morning Brief is written before the operator starts work.

volumes.name: proofrun-memory
volumes.$volume_note: File-based memory is the source of truth and must survive between runs. Without this, learnings.md resets nightly and the agent stops learning — the one thing this job exists to accumulate.

volumes.name: proofrun-artifacts
volumes.$volume_note: Screenshots, generated pages and run traces, so the Proof screen can render overnight runs the next morning.

observability.$alert_note: jobs/nightly.js exits 1 only when every prospect in the batch failed verification, which is the condition worth waking someone for. A partial batch exits 0 and is reported in the Morning Brief.

$safety_note: This job has no send capability. agent/send-adapter.js throws if called, and no SMTP or email API client exists in the image. Everything it produces waits for a human on the Approve screen.
